title: Mali Federation
capsule: This entry covers the polity at the bend of the Niger that became the modern Republic of Mali. It began as the Mali Federation, a union of the French Soudan and Senegal that gained independence from France on 20 June 1960; when Senegal seceded on 20 August 1960, the remaining Soudanese territory proclaimed itself the Republic of Mali on 22 September 1960 under Modibo Keïta. The republic endured a 1968 coup that installed Moussa Traoré, a 1991 transition to multiparty democracy, and a 2012 northern insurgency and coup, and remains the successor state occupying this territory today. The 1960 start and present-day end date reflect this continuous Malian state rather than the short-lived federation that gave it its name.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The federation's territorial extent is well-defined as the combined territories of French Soudan and Senegal; the anomalous to-date of 2025 suggests the Cliopatria geometry continues into the Republic of Mali era.
